name: Florist

pf.license.need: Floral design and a flower shop: no state license in most places. The business registration, and a seller's permit for sales tax where the state's form asks for one. Plant care that treats plants for pests: a pest control license for the company and an applicator license for each plant tech, where the state's rules require them. All from the state's form.
pf.license.who holds it: The business holds its registration, any seller's permit and any pest control license. Each plant tech holds their own applicator license. Designers hold no license of their own.
what to ask: The seller's permit number, where the state's form asks for one
The company's pest control license, if it treats plants for pests
Each plant tech's applicator license, in their invite reply
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.renewals: A reminder 30 days before a permit, a license or the insurance runs out. Once one lapses, the services it covers pause.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance on file, with its end date. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them before setup (B4-70).
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.

danger words: A fire, or open flame near flowers
A gas smell at the venue
A bad allergic reaction, like trouble breathing
pf.safety.what Rosie says: Danger now: get everyone out, and call 911. No booking until it's safe. A candle fire that's already out gets the safety steps first, then the booking goes on: keep candles away from the flowers, and call 911 if smoke comes back.
pf.safety.grief and crisis: Sympathy orders often come in grief. Crisis words get the 988 and 911 message, and no order goes on in that chat.
pf.safety.pets: A pet that ate a plant (lilies are dangerous for cats): Rosie gives no advice. It says to call a vet or a pet poison line now.
pf.safety.at the venue: Nothing is hung on an unsafe hook. Candles sit in glass, where the venue allows them. Nothing blocks an exit or a sprinkler.

pf.first_steps.wedding: A free consultation first (45 minutes, at the shop, by video, or $75 at the venue). Then the proposal holds the date for 7 days, and signing it with the 30% deposit books the wedding. The final count is due 30 days before.
pf.first_steps.installation: A free venue walk-through before a flower wall or hanging pieces, and the venue's written OK where it asks.
pf.first_steps.prep in the reminder: The venue's side door or loading door open at the setup time; candles in glass. For a consultation: bring photos you love, and the venue's rules if you have them.

pf.visit.check-in: An event: the code at the venue's door, from whoever meets the designer (the customer, or the venue's contact for the day). A consultation: the code at the shop's desk, or read out at the start by video. A pickup: the code at the counter. A delivery to a funeral home, an office or a recipient: no code; DONE with a photo, and the sender gets the photo.
pf.visit.nobody there for a delivery: The driver calls the number once, and brings the flowers back the next morning, free. A second miss: Sam decides.
pf.visit.changes on the day: More pieces need the customer's written yes, at list prices, paid by one pay link. A stand-in flower agreed in the contract is used as written; anything else needs a new yes.
pf.visit.done: DONE with photos of the setup. Loaned vases are counted at pickup, at the time the venue set. A missing one is a fee only with Sam's yes.
pf.visit.right to cancel: Extras placed at a venue get a right to cancel only where the state's rules say so.

pf.money.events: Quoted from the plan, with a signed contract. A 25% deposit when booked (a wedding: a 30% deposit at signing that holds the date). The rest is paid on the bill after the event (a wedding: on the bill after the wedding). Nothing is charged on a set day. The state's caps on deposits win (from the state's form).
pf.money.deliveries and pickups: Paid in full when ordered. Free to cancel until noon the day before (the shop: 24 hours before pickup). After that, the flowers are made, so the price may be kept, only with Sam's yes. No answer in 24 hours: a full refund.
pf.money.wedding cancel schedule (the example's o: 90 days or more before: all back, except a fee of up to $250, never more than what was paid. 21 to 89 days: the deposit is kept. Under 21 days: everything paid is kept. Sam confirms every kept amount. If the business cancels, everything comes back.
pf.money.loaned vases: No hold. $18 for each vase not returned (the example's own), only with Sam's yes, by one pay link.
pf.money.tips: A tip line on a bill only if Sam turns it on.
pf.money.tax: Sales tax on flowers where the state's form says so (the seller's permit switch).
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Yes: both companies pay Rosfield's $2 for each confirmed booking.

never in a text: The name of the person who died
pf.messages.sympathy: Texts to a sympathy sender are short and gentle: no exclamation marks, no rating, no offers, and no 'book again'. They name only what's needed: the funeral home, the day and the time.
pf.messages.recipients: The person who gets the flowers gets no texts: they never agreed to them. Only the driver calls their number, and only to deliver.

pf.staff.skills: Luca leads quoted events and does plant care. Felix does sympathy pieces, deliveries and setups. Elliot leads consultations and custom pieces at the shop, and Hazel does everyday work at the counter.
pf.staff.licenses: Designers hold no license of their own. Plant techs hold an applicator license where the state's rules require one (Luca; Reese, who joins later).
pf.staff.who may OK: Sam OKs every wedding and every quote over $500. Pat may OK Lee Floral Design prices over $500; Sam's answer wins.
pf.staff.stand-in: For an event on a date that can't move: a lead designer Sam trusts from outside the team (Petra Lund), or a full refund.
pf.staff.crews: A large setup may need two designers and the van.

pf.rules.contract: Every event quoted from the plan has a written contract both sign before any money: each piece, the stand-in flowers if one is short, the loaned pieces and their fees, and the dated cancel schedule.
pf.rules.venue rules: Setup and pickup times, open flame, what can hang and the loading door come from the venue, for each booking. A venue may ask for the insurance certificate first.
pf.rules.right to cancel: For extras sold at a home, where the state's rules say so.
pf.rules.delivery area: 25 miles from the business; same-day delivery when ordered by noon.

pf.edges.a date that can't move: A wedding or an event: a stand-in lead designer with the skill, or a full refund (B7-54).
pf.edges.a flower short at the wholesaler: The stand-in agreed in the contract is used, at the same price; anything else needs the customer's new yes (B7-34).
pf.edges.the final count: Due 30 days before a wedding. A late count leaves the order as signed (B7-x01).
pf.edges.rain on an outdoor ceremony: The venue's rain plan: the same flowers move inside, with no extra fee (B7-35, B8-31).
pf.edges.a van in traffic: The customer hears only if the flowers won't be set up by the start (B7-18).
pf.edges.nobody there for a delivery: One call, then a free redelivery the next morning (B8-17).
pf.edges.a sympathy service moves: The sender hears the new delivery time first; Sam confirms it with the funeral home (B4-x01).
pf.edges.a missing loaned vase: Sam decides the fee, never more than the contract says (B10-21).
pf.edges.an unsafe hook: Nothing is hung; the customer gets a written note (B8-30).
pf.edges.crisis words: The 988 and 911 message, and no order in that chat.

Renames: the example's haircut, barber, cut, color, kids cut, skin fade, perm, catering, plumbing words renamed to flower words; "delivery fee", "leak", "color" kept (real here: delivery charges, a leak in a privacy rule, flower colors).

Children: no child-left split is turned off here (the plug-in keeps the master's parent-stays rule); kids are not booked alone.
